title: Didn't Sleep Enough Exercise May Protect Your Memory
paragraphs: Everyone knows that a bad night's sleep can make it harder to think clearly and remember things. However, a new study from Canada suggests that a short workout may help protect your memory after a sleepless night, just as well as a nap.

The study was published in the journal PNAS in August 2026. It was led by Madhura Lotlikar and Marc Roig, researchers at McGill University in Montreal. The study involved 53 healthy young adults, who were asked to stay awake in a laboratory for 30 hours in a row.

After that, the participants were divided into three groups. One group exercised on a stationary bike for 20 minutes at a moderate pace. Another group was allowed to take a 90-minute nap in a quiet, dark room. The third group sat on a stationary bike for 20 minutes without pedaling.

Next, all the participants looked at 150 pictures while the researchers recorded their brain activity. Three days later, they were given a surprise test. They were shown the original pictures mixed with 75 new ones and asked which pictures they had seen before.

The results showed that both exercise and napping helped. The exercise group correctly recognized 56% of the original pictures, and the nap group recognized 57%. In contrast, the group that did not exercise or nap recognized only 46%.

Interestingly, the two activities seemed to work in different ways. The nap helped the brain recover from tiredness. Exercise did not reduce tiredness, but it helped the brain use its remaining energy more efficiently while learning.

However, the researchers stressed that exercise cannot replace sleep. In addition, the study only looked at one night without sleep, which may be different from the long-term sleep problems that many people have.
Still, the researchers believe that exercise may help people perform better when getting enough sleep is not possible.
